runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter at 10f on good ground (0W3P in similar conditions), races prominently and will look to secure a handy position from stall 9; veteran at 10 years old but clearly still competitive at this level and trip.

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who sets the pace from stall 1, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.94] flag is a significant caution — it is racing out of its natural role and its chance in shapes that rely on this position should be discounted accordingly; 0W2P in similar going over comparable trips.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse at heart whose recent form includes a break and a very short 3-day turnaround — freshness is a query; mapped to midfield due to hold-up congestion but will naturally want to race further back than the map shows, and the [STYLE_FIT] flag warns against expecting it to perform if unable to get its preferred position.

runners_data.name: Three Yorkshiremen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form has been set largely on softer or standard ground — the switch to good at Bath may not be a concern but the step back up in trip to 1m3½f after several shorter outings is worth noting; trainer Jack Jones has one win from 18 runners over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Arundel
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old from Ed Dunlop's yard, rated OR 65 and top weight, whose limited recent history shows placed form on soft; hold-up style suits this scenario if Grey Fox sets a soft pace, and amateur jockey Mr Henry Callan will need to time the run perfectly.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type aged 11 with a win over 17f on good ground in recent history and placed form at 16f — the step up to 1m3½f at Bath may actually suit; trainer Bernard Llewellyn has one win from 10 runners in 14 days, a positive stable indicator.

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection, racing from a midfield base with exceptional consistency on good ground (0W4P from five runs, all placed); the stable has one win from five runners over 14 days and the horse's form string of 343232 screams consistent performer waiting for the right opportunity.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Archie Watson's yard who has registered 0W0P in three runs on good ground over 12f — the going switch here is not a concern but results have been uninspiring; trainer Archie Watson is in decent form with four wins from 19 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Olly Murphy who has faced varied surfaces and distances; hg:v suggests headgear is a factor, and the amateur rider Mr Josh Myers carries a 7lb claim which is a practical benefit, though 0W0P on good ground over comparable trips limits enthusiasm.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Fox is the one confirmed front runner in this nine-runner field and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m3½f Bath trip on good ground. Three Yorkshiremen and Revich will push forward to dispute prominent positions, while The Pug is another who wants to race handy — meaning the early order may be more competitive for those forward berths than the single pace-setter suggests. Applejack Poet is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to the congestion of hold-up horses at the rear; its true running style is off the pace, but it is unlikely to be as far back as it would prefer. With Grey Fox setting a measured, uncontested tempo, the shape strongly favours patients, well-handicapped closers who can travel in behind and pick off a tiring leader in the final two furlongs, rewarding those in the Midfield-to-Hold-Up band who settle efficiently and produce a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Fox Controls, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Fox sets a steady, uncontested pace and the field strings out behind, allowing closers to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Grey Fox's lone front-running role on a flat, galloping Bath track creates a false-tempo situation where the race turns into a test of stamina and finishing kick in the final quarter-mile; horses who have been racing prominently will have used energy early while true closers arrive fresh.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Pair Held On
scenarios.trigger: If Revich and Three Yorkshiremen push the tempo hard enough early to stretch the field, leaving front-rank types vulnerable but also stopping closers from mounting a clean sweep.
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop suits any horse that can race prominently without over-committing, turning it into a test of class and tactical positioning rather than a pure stamina grind; Revich's consistent placed form at similar distances on good ground makes it the principal beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Field Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a wave of horses from the back arrive simultaneously, producing a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: Shahbaz and Arundel, both racing patiently from the rear, could benefit if the front-rank horses empty simultaneously; Arundel's youth and OR of 65 give it a class edge if it can find a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Fox is allowed to go so slowly in front that it completely conserves its energy and outstays all challengers coming from behind.
scenarios.body: This requires the pace to be genuinely dawdling and the hold-up horses to be caught flat-footed in the straight — an unlikely but not impossible scenario given the field's amateur jockeys and potential tactical inexperience; Grey Fox's [STYLE_FIT] flag tempers confidence significantly.

watchPoints.text: Grey Fox's [STYLE_FIT=0.94] flag is the race's biggest tactical alarm — if it races further back than expected or fails to assert early, the entire pace map dissolves and the race becomes a sprint finish from an uncontested midfield.

Three Yorkshiremen and Revich both want prominent positions from wide draws (7 and 9) and could create a brief but meaningful pace duel with Grey Fox in the opening furlongs, which would significantly benefit closers Stintino Sunset and Cogital.

Stintino Sunset's draw in stall 2 is advantageous for a midfield runner — watch whether Mr Ross Birkett takes advantage early to sit just off the pace rather than being forced wide, as track position here could be decisive.

Cogital's history includes a win at 17f on good ground (1W from 11 similar-going runs) — at 1m3½f this is its shortest recent assignment, and if the race develops into a strong-pace stamina test it could be underestimated at its OR of 50.

Three amateur jockeys carrying claims (Miss Georgia King 5lb, Miss Imogen Mathias 3lb, Mr Kieran Wood 7lb, Mr Josh Myers 7lb) add tactical unpredictability — positional errors in the early stages on Bath's long run-in could materially alter the race shape.

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran operating well out of his comfort zone on this flat turf trip — one win from many over longer AW trips and a sparse turf record on similar going offers little encouragement at 1m2f on this surface; drawn wide in stall 6, he is likely to be held up midfield without the tactical pace to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Dialstone
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has run only twice but both efforts were placings — including a second on Good ground at 10f — and Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride for a yard firing at 9/47 in the 14-day window; 38 days between runs is not a concern for Beckett, and draw 2 is ideal for a horse likely to stalk the pace throughout.

runners_data.name: Colonnade
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's runner brings the highest OR in the field (79) and is the lone pace-setter, but has raced exclusively over sprint trips on the AW — stepping markedly up to 1m2f on turf represents a significant shift; STYLE_FIT flag is noted, meaning the prominent tag should be treated with some caution as this is a new role at a new distance.

runners_data.name: Mathoura
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's three-year-old has placed twice over 10f on Good ground and arrives fresh off a 14-day turnaround — the apprentice claimer Mason Paetel (3) takes the ride which brings a 3lb allowance; a prominent position suits but the Going-form combination shows a mixed record (one place from four similar outings), making reliability the key question.

runners_data.name: Soul Of Appin
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's four-year-old is completely unexposed — no days-since-last-run data, going listed as UNKNOWN, and style unclassified — making assessment very difficult; Meehan has a modest 3/11 in the 14-day window and stall 1 could be an asset if the horse has natural early pace, but this is a genuine unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Indian Mary
runners_data.note: Philippart De Foy's filly carries a "fades in finish" flag which is deeply concerning in a race that is likely to be settled by a sharp effort in the Bath straight; her sole run produced an eighth from 10f on AW, and 44 days off combined with the finishing concern makes her the most speculative runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Colonnade is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no rival pressing from the front, is set to control a measured, uncontested gallop over Bath's 1m2f on Good turf. Mathoura and Dialstone both carry prominent-to-midfield profiles and are likely to sit in behind the leader without disrupting the tempo, meaning the pace will be sustainable rather than searching. With only one genuine pace-setter dictating at a comfortable clip, the race is unlikely to develop into a true stamina test; instead, a smooth, well-judged gallop will compress the field entering the straight, leaving the outcome to be settled by a short, sharp finish. This shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can travel close to the pace and pick up efficiently in the closing stages — the midfield-to-prominent profile, exemplified by Dialstone, is ideally placed to exploit an uncontested, controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dialstone Controls Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Colonnade bowls along uncontested and the pace remains honest but not punishing, setting up a clean straight-line finish.
scenarios.body: Dialstone, sitting just off the leader from draw 2, travels within striking distance throughout and can deploy a measured late kick on Ground the form book shows suits; two placings in two runs on Good or faster confirms the profile fits perfectly here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mathoura Runs On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly quicker than expected and Dialstone is unable to sustain its effort, leaving Mathoura to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Mathoura has placed twice over 10f on Good ground and, ridden prominently by the claimer Paetel, can travel handily and aim a straight finish at the leader; a faster-than-anticipated early tempo would suit its grinding style over rivals who might over-race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Colonnade Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that Colonnade's uncontested lead proves impossible to reel in entering the short Bath straight.
scenarios.body: Colonnade leads without a rival engaging, conserves energy fully in the early stages, and the six-runner field fails to organise a meaningful chase until too late; the short run-in at Bath limits the time available for closers to respond.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Gate Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Of Appin or No Ordinary Joe produce a career-best on a flat, fair track with unknown or lightly exposed form providing a wildcard.
scenarios.body: Soul Of Appin is completely unknown on going and style, and No Ordinary Joe has shown a one-win-from-many profile suggesting inconsistency; either could surprise only if rivals fail to run their races in a truly honest finish.

watchPoints.text: Dialstone's jumping position from stall 2 is critical — if Rhys Clutterbuck slots directly in behind Colonnade in the first furlong, Dialstone controls its own race and is perfectly placed to challenge; a poor break or wide early route would compromise that tactical advantage.

Colonnade's ability to stay 1m2f on turf is entirely unproven after three sprint runs on AW — if the horse ties up or fades markedly inside the final two furlongs, it could bring the field through in a rush and compress the finish unpredictably.

Mathoura's claimer Mason Paetel (3) is worth monitoring in the early stages — if Paetel elects to be more aggressive than expected and pushes Colonnade for the lead, the pace dynamic changes entirely and suits hold-up horses rather than the prominent types.

Soul Of Appin (stall 1) is completely unknown — watch the pre-race market move carefully; any significant market support for a horse with no visible form data would be a meaningful signal given Meehan's ability to place a fresh horse to maximum effect.

Indian Mary's "fades in finish" flag means watch her position entering the final 2f — if she has tracked the pace and begins to weaken sharply, it will signal the pace was genuinely demanding and act as a useful reference point for assessing Mathoura's finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Cracking Idea
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's runner has placed form at 7f on Good ground (5th and 3rd) and steps up to a mile, but is a natural hold-up horse whose deep-closing style is compromised here because the rear of the field is overcrowded — likely to race further forward than ideal, which tempers its chance.

runners_data.name: Biscaysian
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's juvenile has two runs on Good ground (4th at 8f, 5th at 7f) and a step up to a mile with a prominent style from draw 3 suits perfectly; Jack Callan takes the ride and this horse profiles as the most natural fit for the tactical shape this race will take.

runners_data.name: Baarberini
runners_data.note: James Horton's OR 75 rated runner has back-to-back placed efforts (3rd and 2nd) over 7-8f on Standard and is the most experienced handicap-rated runner in the field; Daniel Muscutt from draw 7 allows a smooth midfield position and the mile on Good should suit.

runners_data.name: Able Tasman
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's front-running two-year-old steps back up to a mile after a third at 7f on Good and has had a 105-day break; Jack Mitchell will look to use draw 4 to press on from the gun, and how well this horse has progressed over the summer break is the critical unknown.

runners_data.name: Yabreen
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's runner was a beaten seventh over 6f on Good last time and the step up to a mile looks necessary; a hold-up style from draw 6 in a field with too many closers means finding clear daylight will be a challenge, and early pace experience is limited.

runners_data.name: Orchard Hatches
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's front-runner has placed form at 8f on Good (3rd) but was also beaten 8th at 7f on Good; drawn 12, Rhys Clutterbuck will need to push across to maintain a prominent berth from a wide stall, and if this horse is outgunned early by Able Tasman the plan unravels.

runners_data.name: Deira Moon
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's debutant at Bath ran 7th over 7f on Standard and carries a finish-fades warning; the step up to a mile from draw 5 could help stamina, but the hold-up style and that fade flag combine to make this one hard to trust at this stage.

runners_data.name: The Sergeon
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's runner was 5th on Good over 8f at Kempton and is a hold-up type from draw 10; Jack Dace (5lb claimer) takes the ride and in a race with so many closers all seeking a similar late position, finding a clear run will be the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Starlight Bay
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's filly carries a finish-fades flag and was a distant 11th on Soft over 8f; the switch to Good ground and a drop in trip to one mile could help, but a hold-up style and the fade concern make it hard to see her competitive from draw 2.

runners_data.name: Naseebwali
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's runner is a debutant with no public form and going is listed as UNKNOWN; the lightly-raced flag and absence of any form string means this is pure speculation territory — Dylan Hogan from draw 8 will need to find a rhythm quickly if this horse is to feature.

runners_data.name: Boomshakalak
runners_data.note: Zoe Hawkins's runner ran 7th over 7f on Good and is a natural hold-up type with a fade flag; the trainer's limited 14-day strike rate (0/1) is noted, and like Cracking Idea this horse's deepest-closing instincts are displaced by the overpopulated hold-up division — racing further forward than natural is not guaranteed to help.

runners_data.name: Greta Tintin
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's prominent runner has struggled (13th and 9th on Soft and Standard) and carries wide draw 14 from which William Carver will need to work to establish position; Balding's strong 14-day record (13/69) is an angle, but the form figures offer little confidence at this point.

runners_data.name: Trispen
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's debutant has no public form and an UNKNOWN going tag; Stevie Donohoe from draw 11 will need this horse to show natural ability on debut, and with a strong 14-day strike rate (3/14) Burrows occasionally produces a live newcomer — completely unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Mulvaney's Return
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's prominent runner has a useful form string (3rd at 8f Soft, 6th at 8f Good) and the mile trip is established; Liam Wright (3lb claimer) from draw 9 can slot into a handy spot, and of the proven runners who suit the prominent-to-handy profile this horse has the most relevant recent evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Orchard Hatches and Able Tasman are the two confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field, and with both likely to press for early position from draws 12 and 4 respectively, there will be a genuine contested gallop from the outset over Bath's one-mile trip. The early duel between these two will set an honest, sustainable pace that stretches the field, making it hard for anything tardy off the bridle to land a telling blow from the rear. Prominent racers who can settle just off the front pair — Biscaysian and Mulvaney's Return — are best placed to capitalise as the pace setters may tire in the straight, while true hold-up horses face a stern test if the gallop is strong enough to compress the field. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Cracking Idea and Boomshakalak are genuine closers who have been mapped into midfield purely because the rear is over-subscribed, meaning neither is likely to secure their natural position — Biscaysian and Greta Tintin are better placed to fill the prominent slots. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours the prominent-to-handy profile, horses who can travel smoothly in second or third early and deliver a controlled challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Orchard Hatches and Able Tasman press each other genuinely from the off and the race is run at a strong, honest clip throughout.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off, leaving the prominent stalkers — Biscaysian and Mulvaney's Return — ideally placed to swoop in the final two furlongs with fresh legs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Able Tasman gains a clear advantage early and is allowed to bowl along uncontested or in front at a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Able Tasman settles into a rhythm and, with reserves in the tank, quickens away from the field in the straight before rivals can respond; a controlled gallop suits a horse with scope for improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to soften the front two, allowing a well-positioned midfield runner to pick them off close home.
scenarios.body: Baarberini, who has shown progressive placed form over this trip, can travel smoothly through the middle of the pack and produce a sustained challenge in the straight; a truly-run race plays to stamina over raw speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is exceptionally strong and the entire prominent group fades, opening a late window for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Cracking Idea or Boomshakalak, though both are likely to be racing out of their natural rearmost position given the crowded hold-up contingent, would need an unusually strong gallop and a clear passage to land a challenge from the rear; this is the least likely shape given both are redistributed rather than truly settled at the back.

watchPoints.text: Able Tasman vs Orchard Hatches — watch how aggressively Orchard Hatches from draw 12 pushes across to contest the lead; if the two front-runners are locked in a duel as early as the 6f pole, the pace will be strong enough to compromise both and open the race for prominent stalkers.

Cracking Idea and Boomshakalak are both genuine hold-up horses who may find themselves racing further forward than ideal given the overcrowded rear; if either drifts wide seeking a run in the straight it could cause interference for horses in the midfield group including Baarberini and The Sergeon.

Greta Tintin (draw 14) — watch the first furlong to see whether William Carver elects to push wide and force a prominent position or accepts a midfield berth; if trapped wide on the turn at Bath, that energy cost can prove decisive against younger rivals on a track where the bend is significant.

Naseebwali and Trispen are both debutants with no public form whose unknown styles add genuine uncertainty to the pace map — either could emerge as a natural front-runner and further crowd the early pace, or alternatively drop in and swell the hold-up group even further.

Baarberini holds the only published OR (75) in the field — watch whether that handicap mark reflects a genuine class edge over unexposed rivals; if Muscutt tracks the pace efficiently from draw 7, this horse could prove the value benchmark against which the unrated runners are measured in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Amber Ocean is the confirmed lone front-runner and will stride for the lead from stall 8, a high draw at Bath where low numbers are favoured, meaning she will need to work across early to establish position — that effort may blunt her finish even if she secures the rail. Four horses — Dowman, Perigord Noir, Space Dreamer, and Pj's Corner — all carry prominent pace profiles and will contest the second rank immediately behind Amber Ocean, creating a compressed early order with genuine traffic risk two to three furlongs out as they jostle for position on the climb through the home straight. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can comfortably accommodate: of those, Perigord Noir from stall 2 (favoured) and Dowman from stall 4 (neutral) are best placed geographically to slot in just behind the leader without burning fuel crossing the track, while Space Dreamer and Pj's Corner from high draws will be hustling early and may end up racing wider than ideal. Good ground, a sustained uphill finish at Bath, and a genuine if unforced early tempo collectively favour horses who can travel prominently with cover and produce a strong staying kick through the final furlong — the prominent-from-a-low-draw profile is the clear tactical winner here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Ocean bowls along at a sustainable pace and Perigord Noir tracks closely from stall 2, the race sets up as a procession for horses sitting second or third throughout.
scenarios.body: Perigord Noir, ideally positioned from a favoured draw with a horse in front to follow, can pounce as Amber Ocean ties up on the hill; the sustained Good ground rewards those who travel in rhythm rather than sprint from cover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Amber Ocean crosses cleanly to the rail, establishes an uncontested lead, and the pace remains genuinely even rather than fast, she could simply outstay all pursuers up the Bath hill.
scenarios.body: A lone leader on Good ground who is never seriously pressured through the first two furlongs can conserve enough energy to resist the late challenge from prominent horses; Amber Ocean's 1W2P record on similar ground underlines she handles this surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: High-draw scramblers disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types from high draws — Space Dreamer, Pj's Corner, South West — push forward aggressively early and create a faster-than-expected tempo, the race turns messy and a fresher-legged midfield type can capitalise.
scenarios.body: Penny Capri, dropping in OR and carrying a 5f win on Good ground from stall 3 (favoured), would be the beneficiary as the early chaos burns off those in front; Knock Three Times, with a similar midfield profile, is the secondary threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the entire prominent pack over-races and ties up simultaneously on the hill, a hold-up horse arriving late could benefit — but this depends largely on Jazz Queen producing a career-best or Birkacre Brow (a natural prominent type redistributed to the rear) finding a clear passage.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally weak because the sole true hold-up runner, Jazz Queen, has a losing streak on Good ground and no win at the trip, while Birkacre Brow is not genuinely at home racing from behind and its style fit is discounted accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Amber Ocean's high draw (stall 8) is the pivotal early watch — if she fails to cross cleanly to the rail in the first two furlongs, she concedes the favoured ground to Perigord Noir and Dowman and her chance of leading comfortably evaporates.

Stall congestion from Pj's Corner (10), Space Dreamer (9), and South West (7) could produce a scramble for position in the first furlong, elevating the pace well above what Amber Ocean alone would set and fundamentally reshaping the scenario probabilities.

Perigord Noir has not won in five career starts — watch whether Jack Dace (5lb claimer) positions him immediately off Amber Ocean's back through the first two furlongs, as any hesitation or wide berth from stall 2 would waste the draw advantage that underpins his top selection status.

South West's first-time blinkers are an unknown quantity: if they over-sharpen him he could contest the lead unexpectedly, adding genuine pace pressure to a race expected to feature only one true front-runner and altering the tempo calculation for every horse behind.

Bath's 5f rises steeply through the final furlong — watch how quickly Amber Ocean's stride shortens approaching the two-pole, as any sign of laboured running at that point is the clearest signal that prominent horses travelling smoothly behind her are about to take command.

races.paceDynamic: Smith and Lady Lauren are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this stamina-testing 2m1f trip at Bath, creating an honest, contested gallop that is unlikely to collapse into a crawl. With Good ground and a genuine pace duel up front, the tempo should be sustained enough to stretch the field out early and set up a proper staying test in the straight. That profile most favours a horse who can travel prominently just off the pace without burning reserves — a confirmed midfield stalker who can pick off the leaders when they cry enough. Fram Castle, mapped to midfield with a recent win at 14f on Good and strong trainer form, is ideally placed to exploit that shape. Note also that this field carries a heavy concentration of genuine hold-up types (La Trinite, Fornido, Cherry Cola, N'Ion) that have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear is oversubscribed — in reality they will likely be crowded toward the back and will need an unusually strong gallop to generate sufficient momentum for a late run, which the pace duel does at least provide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Smith and Lady Lauren fight it out up front at a genuine clip and the midfield stalkers travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: The pace duel softens both leaders before the final quarter-mile, leaving the race to horses who have tracked them at a measured distance without emptying their tanks; Fram Castle's recent 14f win on Good and proven ability to settle and quicken makes this profile the most natural fit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Steals
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners takes control unchallenged after Smith or Lady Lauren cracks and the early tempo drops to a crawl.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn gallop rewards whoever controls the race from the front, and the horse that seizes the initiative can find a second wind in the straight with rivals flat-footed; Lady Lauren, young and lightly burdened at 118lbs, is the more likely beneficiary if she gets it soft.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop, Late Closers Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is genuinely strong enough to burn off midfield horses and only the true hold-up runners have enough left in the tank.
scenarios.body: A lung-busting gallop set by the front pair could theoretically drag the late runners into contention, but the redistributed closers — Fornido, La Trinite, Cherry Cola — will need to have genuinely settled deeper than their natural position suggests; Fornido's consistent placed form gives it the best claims here if the race falls truly truly fast.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Affair, Any Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uneven and fragmented, with early positional scrapping among the large hold-up contingent disrupting normal race order.
scenarios.body: A 12-runner field with multiple horses forced wide of their preferred spots creates a ragged race where position in running counts for little; any runner that secures a comfortable, untroubled midfield berth early — such as Simiyann or Cloudy Rose — could sneak into contention at a rewarding price.

watchPoints.text: Fram Castle (draw 2) will push forward from a low draw to settle just off the pace — watch whether Alexandra Egan gets the split she needs tracking Smith and Lady Lauren early, because if she is trapped wide or checked it compromises the winning shape entirely.

Smith (68 days off, stall 7) has a long absence to overcome as the presumed co-pace-setter — if he misses the break or shows race-rustiness, Lady Lauren could find herself alone on the front end and control the tempo unchallenged, materially shifting the race shape toward Scenario B.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (La Trinite, Fornido, Cherry Cola, N'Ion) will all be hunting the same patch of ground at the rear early; watch for scrimmaging in the first half-mile that leaves any of them without cover or unbalanced before the field settles.

Simiyann (headgear: tongue-tie and blinkers) has the most consistent placed record at trips around 2m on Good ground — if it gets a clean midfield passage from stall 4 it could outrun its odds as a secondary beneficiary of the contested-pace scenario.

Turton's trip record (all starts at 8-12f) is the single biggest unknown in the race — monitor market moves close to post as any stable confidence about the step to 2m1f would be a meaningful signal given the absence of stamina evidence in the formbook.

runners_data.name: Alshimali
runners_data.note: Sole winner on good going in this field (1/5f/GOO in form) gives her strong going credentials, but stall 6 is against the low-draw bias and Josephine Gordon will need a generous tempo to coax a late run from this hold-up type; the wide draw is a genuine structural disadvantage at Bath.

runners_data.name: Trafalger
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner who will set the sole pace from stall 5, but a record of 5-5-8-5-3 on good and good-to-soft with zero wins in six similar-going starts makes her a tone-setter rather than a winning proposition; tongue-tie noted.

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's hold-up filly drops to a career-low OR of 53 and gets the benefit of stall 2 on the favoured low draw, but five consecutive placed-or-beaten efforts over 6f on good ground without a win or placing makes improvement hard to argue with confidence.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's mare has a solid record of 1W3P from ten good-ground starts and ran well in both her second-placed efforts over 6f on good, but stall 3 is only neutral and her midfield style means she needs the pace to stack up ahead of her to produce a clean late challenge.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted on OR 52 with a recent run just 10 days ago, but a genuine hold-up horse whose wide draw in stall 8 pushes them against the structural bias and out of their preferred last-to-first role in a field that already has several horses wanting cover; the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag reflects that racing near midfield rather than at the rear will blunt their effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who has placed four times from 15 good-ground starts and will look to occupy a prominent position from stall 4, directly complementing Macarone's rail position; Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim is a tangible weight aid on OR 49, and the horse's recent consistency (four places from six) makes them a reliable each-way type.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Ben Ffrench Davis's 5lb claim helps on a low mark of OR 51 and stall 1 hands Grace Harris's horse the rail on a course and going combination where she has won and placed repeatedly (1W2P from 15 good-ground runs); the prominent style and draw alignment make her structurally the best-placed runner in the race.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's runner drops sharply in class and grade from longer trips — all recent history is over 7f-8f — and the flagged tendency to fade in the finish makes a 5½f dash on good ground a significant test of stamina in reverse; stall 7 adds a further draw disadvantage on top of the profile mismatch.

races.paceDynamic: Trafalger is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 5, will look to dictate from the off at a sustainable gallop with no natural rival to press them — this is a controlled, single-pace lead rather than a scorched-earth sprint. Some Nightmare and Macarone will push forward from stalls 4 and 1 respectively to occupy the prominent positions just behind, with Macarone's favoured low draw giving her a clean pitch on the rail. The hold-up horses — Alshimali, May Encounter, and Ten Club — will settle in behind the tempo, but because this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, Ten Club in particular is likely to find themselves racing further forward than their natural style; Alshimali and May Encounter are the true closers. A single honest pacer setting a measured tempo over 5½f at Bath's uphill finish on good ground favours those racing prominently or just off the pace — specifically prominent types with a late gear who won't be buried in traffic, making Macarone and Some Nightmare's forward positions structurally ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Macarone Controls From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Macarone uses stall 1 to grab the rail and sit just behind Trafalger, allowing a controlled tempo and sprinting clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Macarone's favoured low draw and recent good-ground win over 6f put her perfectly positioned to benefit from a single uncontested pacer, tracking before unleashing a turn of foot on the uphill climb. The prominent-style horses dominate as hold-up runners struggle to reel in a well-rated, well-placed winner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Trafalger sets a genuinely sustainable fraction and the hold-up horses fail to close on the uphill finish.
scenarios.body: Trafalger dictates on their own terms, and with no rival to force a burn-up, they conserve enough to resist at a moderate pace over an undemanding 5½f circuit. Prominent horses who track Trafalger could inherit places if the closers stall, elevating Some Nightmare and Be An Angel for the minor money.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Power Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Trafalger goes too quick early and the pace collapses inside the final two furlongs, opening the track for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Alshimali, drawn wide in stall 6 but boasting the sole win in similar going in this field, would have most to gain with a strong late run if the early tempo bites into the front-runners' reserves. May Encounter's favoured low-to-middle draw in stall 2 gives her a clear route to the stands rail if the gaps open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If crowding off the stalls causes positional disruption and no horse gets a clear passage until far too late.
scenarios.body: With several hold-up types circling the same real estate in a tight 8-runner field, a muddled mid-race traffic scenario could scramble the form book — Be An Angel, who has repeatedly placed in good ground, might find daylight at the right moment. Rock Master, though habitually fading, could at least feature briefly from an outside draw if the field strings out unusually wide.

watchPoints.text: Macarone (stall 1) will attempt to monopolise the rail behind Trafalger — if she secures that position cleanly in the first furlong, every other runner must go around her in the straight.

Trafalger's uncontested lead could be deceptively slow in the first half of the race, compressing the field and making the final-furlong sprint a mass finish — watch the sectional split at the 2f pole.

Ten Club (stall 8) will be racing against both the draw bias and their natural style; a wide, wide passage combined with an out-of-role position in mid-division makes their chance highly conditional on an unusually messy race shape.

Rock Master has run all recent form over 7f-8f on good ground — a drop to 5½f is untested and the finishing-fade flag suggests they may not see it out, but their early pace from stall 7 could briefly disrupt the prominent group.

Alshimali's trainer Tony Carroll has a 5/41 14-day record and also saddles Rock Master — dual-runner scenarios can sometimes produce tactical riding instructions worth watching in the early stages if Alshimali needs a contested pace to land a late blow.

runners_data.name: The Ormer Gatherer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and returning after a 456-day absence for a small trainer with modest recent strike-rate; unknown going profile and complete style uncertainty make it impossible to place with confidence in any race shape.

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: Six-year-old midfield runner for John & Rhys Flint, who have drawn a blank in their last seven outings; has four consecutive placings around the 8f mark on Good ground and the Scorecard tops this horse — the 12-day turnaround and similar-going record of three placings in 14 runs is encouraging without being emphatic.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer in a race that is already saturated with back-markers — bumped out of its natural slot to show as midfield on the map, it is unlikely to find the rear position it needs; seven-year-old sporting a tongue-tie, with no wins or places in seven similar-going runs, and a trainer without a recent winner.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's three-year-old carries top-weight at 137lbs but is the form horse in the field with three wins and five places in seven Good-ground starts including back-to-back wins over 7-8f; the step up to a mile and the weight are the only questions.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: A natural rear-of-field horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the congestion of hold-up types — its true finishing position will be nearer the back than the map implies; seven-year-old with zero wins and only one place in ten similar-going runs, making it hard to trust even if it finds clear air late.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old for the Flint yard, whose trainer is winless in seven recent starts; has shown one placing in seven similar-going attempts and has drifted progressively down in finishing positions over shorter trips, raising concerns about whether the mile genuinely helps.

runners_data.name: Victorian Rose
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old with a tendency to fade in the finish — a significant concern over a flat Bath mile where the straight is long and unforgiving; just three runs on soft-to-standard ground with no placing, and 69 days off the track adds to the profile of a horse that may help set the pace but is unlikely to finish it out.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Three-year-old midfield type with a modest record — nine runs yielding zero wins and one placing across 6-8f on Good and Standard; the going note is fine but the form string of 4-9896 shows a downward trajectory in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Prominent three-year-old drawn in stall 1, giving her the clearest run of any horse in the race; has placed in three of her last five Good-ground starts over 7-8f and her low draw is a concrete positional advantage in this field shape.

runners_data.name: Grand Vista
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's three-year-old hold-up type with two placings in four Good-ground outings; positioned in stall 6 with a useful draw, but the form string of 038368 shows inconsistency and the similar-going record of four runs without a win limits expectations.

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans' five-year-old is the Scorecard's first danger and recent form includes a win on Good over 8f and two further placings; a genuine hold-up horse drawn in stall 4, but similar-going profile of one win and two places from twelve attempts suggests the top is a ceiling rather than a floor.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: Experienced seven-year-old who is a true hold-up performer — the field's volume of rear-runners means it is mapped forward of its natural ground; a perfect 7/7 similar-going record does not include a single win or place in those seven, making it difficult to upgrade on what the form says.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Grace Harris' four-year-old is the second Scorecard danger with strong recent form including a win on Soft and two further 8f Good-ground placings; drawn widest of all in stall 14 which is a headwind on this course, and the step from 7f to a mile remains a minor question.

runners_data.name: Neat And Tidy
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race, but drawn in stall 12 and carrying a style-fit flag — will have to cross from an outside berth to lead, which is workable but not ideal; Richard Hughes' three-year-old has no wins in seven starts and has finished no better than fourth in its last five, so dictating the pace is more likely to soften it up for others than to see it home.

races.paceDynamic: Neat And Tidy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 12 on a track where low-to-mid draws are marginally favoured, will need to work across from the outside to establish the lead — a manageable task in a field of 14 with only Victorian Rose likely to push forward alongside. With just one genuine pace-setter and no serious early pressure anticipated, this race will be run at a honest but controlled gallop on Good ground, producing a single-file procession that rewards horses who can sit just off the pace and deploy a sustained mid-race move rather than a late lunge. The field contains more hold-up types than the back of the map can accommodate: Hopjes, Ravenglass, and Oh So Audacious are natural hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred position and will trade ground for comfort, blunting their finishing effectiveness. In a controlled-tempo, single-pace-setter scenario on a flat Bath mile, the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can track Neat And Tidy at close quarters and pick up off a genuine but unscorching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Neat And Tidy controls a moderate tempo unchallenged and the field settles into a tight-grouped procession.
scenarios.body: Horses sitting just off the leader in the first three to five positions will save enough energy to sprint past an honest but untested gallop in the final two furlongs; this is Bath's most common mile template on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Catch Late Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Neat And Tidy goes too slow early and the race lacks a meaningful mid-race injection, setting up a late sweeping finish.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run contest compresses the field into the final quarter-mile and favours runners who can produce a sharp, sustained burst from the back half of the pack; true hold-up horses with finishing speed benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Caught
scenarios.trigger: If Victorian Rose pushes Neat And Tidy into a faster-than-comfortable early pace and both fade in the straight.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop burns out the lead pair and opens the race wide to horses that settled mid-division and cruise past tired leaders from two furlongs out; midfield runners with strong Good-ground form are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Draw And Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early traffic issues, bunching at the turn, and positional shuffling that scrambles the expected running order.
scenarios.body: Runners who secure clean early positions regardless of style and avoid mid-race crowding emerge; horses with tactical flexibility and low draw numbers who find daylight early profit.

watchPoints.text: Neat And Tidy must cross from stall 12 to secure the lead — watch whether it can establish a clean position by the first bend without being pushed wide, as any scrimmage from Victorian Rose in stall 11 could disrupt the expected orderly pace scenario.

Shes Got The Blues carries 137lbs (top weight) for a five-pound claimer — watch how she travels in the final three furlongs, as any sign of weight telling under Rose Dawes on the long Bath straight would swing the race sharply toward hold-up types.

Angel's Call and A Rose Adaay are both genuine hold-up horses drawn in stalls 4 and 14 respectively — watch how much daylight each secures turning for home, as tight traffic through the bend could cost either their winning chance in a close finish.

Hopjes, Ravenglass, and Oh So Audacious are all true back-markers forced forward on the map — if the pace is slow and they drift even further back than expected, watch whether they can manufacture a run at all on a track that does not typically reward extreme late closers.

The Ormer Gatherer returns after 456 days and has completely unknown going and style profile — watch its behaviour in the stalls and its early position, as an erratic or slowly-away start from stall 2 could cause interference for Arvana Belle (stall 1) and Oh So Audacious (stall 3).

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Steps up significantly in trip from her recent 7f form, which came on Standard and Soft; her one run at 8f on Good produced a win so the distance isn't a concern, but a 15-day gap and a midfield style on a course where early position matters slightly lower her claims — trainer Wintle's yard is quietly placed (1/17 in 14 days).|

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator returning from 52 days off for Ian Williams, who has a 2/27 14-day strike rate suggesting the yard is not yet in peak form; placed twice in three Good-ground miles so the conditions suit, but a patient ride from draw 8 means she needs the pace to collapse late.|

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here, drawn centrally in stall 6 with Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) aboard; her history shows six prior runs on Good ground with just one placing, and her form string of 096553 suggests she sets pace rather than finishes it — danger lies in whether the prominent cluster behind overpowers her turn.|

runners_data.name: Freedom Bay
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection at low confidence; Kieran O'Neill takes over and she won on Good ground over 8f in stall 5 (NEUTRAL), with trainer Hawkins having just one runner in 14 days — low yard momentum but the horse's 1W2P on Good ground and prominent style fits this race shape well.|

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Comfortably the highest-rated horse in the field (OR=55, 135lbs), with two wins and three places from four runs on Good ground — the form profile screams that this horse goes well fresh (34 days off) and on this surface; a hold-up style means she needs a strong pace, but the class edge could compensate.|

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up/prominent type, returning within 12 days with three places from 14 Good-ground runs — experienced but modest and in the twilight of a long career; drawn wide in stall 10, he will need a clear passage and a stop-start gallop to feature.|

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell takes a prominent-style four-year-old into a Good-ground mile from stall 7 (NEUTRAL); placed twice on Soft at 8f but only 1 qualifying run on Good in her 10 recorded, which gives minimal confidence — the six in her recent form string is a red flag in the current race shape.|

runners_data.name: Savvi Row
runners_data.note: Returning from 212 days off — the longest absence in the field — with no Good-ground form in her history (all Standard or Standard-to-Slow); a 3yo on a mark of 46 from stall 14, she will need the race to develop very slowly and early fitness to be in doubt.|

runners_data.name: Mooretown Lad
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who routed into the midfield mapping because the hold-up cluster already fills the rear of the field; six-year-old trained by Wintle (same yard as Thai Princess), with 4/10 placings on Good ground but zero wins — his best runs have come when racing from well off the pace, a role he may not fully secure here.|

runners_data.name: Quite Sweet

runners_data.name: Lady V
runners_data.note: A 3yo hold-up filly on a mark of 48 from stall 11, with no wins and no Good-ground placings from two qualifying runs; four runs total and recent form of 6-869 does not inspire confidence — she is likely to need an experience run at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish (⚠) from stall 1 in Millie Wonnacott's care; a prominent style horse with a finish concern on a course that demands a strong home straight, making him unreliable to win even if he settles close to the pace early on.|

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type for the Birkett yard (1/5 in 14 days), with one placing on Good ground from five runs; drawn in stall 4 (NEUTRAL, low draw, mild advantage) and her 2/7f second on Good over a shorter trip hints at an upward trajectory if the extra furlong suits.|

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Back within two days of his last run — the shortest turnaround in the field — for Mark Rimell from stall 12; a prominent type whose Good-ground form (9th, 7th in two qualifying runs) is poor, and rapid reappearance raises freshness questions despite the low OR of 47.|

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with six prominent-minded horses (Freedom Bay, Eye Of The Water, Amarachi, Rival, Girls Allowed, Coiled) all chasing similar real estate, there will be an early scramble for position before the field settles into a compressed, moderate gallop on Bath's flat mile. The prominent cluster will jostle through the first two furlongs, likely producing a sustainable pace that neither burns off the closers nor creates a true true false-pace collapse — Good ground on the round course amplifies this, rewarding a horse that travels through the pace rather than fights for it. Traffic risks are elevated between the two- and three-furlong pole as the prominent pack concertinas; horses drawn low-to-middle (draws 1-7) sitting just off the pace stand to benefit most from the unobstructed racing room Bath's wide track offers. The race shape — a single leader, honest but unchallenging gallop, moderate tempo — classically favours a prominent horse that can slot in behind Who Is Alice without burning energy and then accelerate on the home straight; pure hold-up horses will need things to go right to deliver their run from deep. Mooretown Lad is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position because the field's rear is already over-subscribed; Who Is Alice, Freedom Bay and Rival are the horses most likely to actually secure their natural prominent berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice sets a controlled pace and one of the prominent stalkers slots in cleanly behind before quickening on the turn.
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader creates an honest but manageable gallop, allowing a prominent type to travel on the bridle and unwind a decisive run without over-committing; Bath's uphill finish is short enough that a horse positioned second or third throughout rarely gets caught.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice gets a soft lead, is never seriously pressed, and the chasing pack cancels each other out in a messy bunch.
scenarios.body: With the prominent group fighting for position behind, Who Is Alice could enjoy an untroubled lead at a gentle pace and simply refuse to be caught; Good ground and the flat mile suits a horse that settles well in front and does not idle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble produces a genuinely strong early tempo that burns off those who over-committed, leaving the race open late.
scenarios.body: A contested front will soften the prominent brigade through the final two furlongs, creating a gap for a hold-up horse with a turn of foot to come through; Desert Charm's strong finishing record on Good ground makes her the stand-out beneficiary if the race truly falls apart up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a dawdle and a hold-up horse manages to squeeze through along the rail from a midfield pitch.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the number of prominent types determined to press forward and the limited probability of a genuine false pace; the scenario depends on crowded circumstances neutralising the front-runners, which Bath's wide track makes less likely than on a narrow track.

watchPoints.text: Six prominent horses (Freedom Bay, Eye Of The Water, Amarachi, Rival, Girls Allowed, Coiled) will contest the same early ground behind Who Is Alice — watch for bumping and checked runs between the 6f and 5f markers as the pack sorts itself out.

Who Is Alice (Harry Vigors, 5lb claimer) must dictate from stall 6 without interference; if the prominent scramble forces her to quicken early, her tendency to not finish suggests she could stop abruptly inside the final furlong and bring down rivals behind her.

Desert Charm arrives as the most exposed horse on form (OR=55, two wins on Good) but is a hold-up type needing the pace to be genuine — monitor betting moves; if she drifts she has not found her race, if she shortens significantly the market believes the tempo will be strong enough.

Savvi Row returns from 212 days off with no Good-ground form and a wide draw (14); she is a potential early rogue element if unfit and may unsettle rhythm in the early stages before dropping out tamely.

Freedom Bay (stall 5, Kieran O'Neill) is best placed of the prominent stalkers in terms of draw and style — watch where she travels in the first two furlongs as a barometer of whether the Strand Scorecard's selection can reach her natural position without burning too much energy.
